title: The World in 2050
description: Make detailed predictions about the future using the future continuous, the future perfect (simple and continuous), and expressions such as be about to, be due to and be likely to. Vocabulary: science, cities and society.
objectives: Describe actions in progress at a future time with the future continuous
Talk about actions completed before a future time with the future perfect
Use be about to, be due to, be likely to and be bound to accurately
Make predictions with different degrees of certainty about science, cities and society

lessons.title: Future Continuous: This Time Tomorrow
lessons.summary: Menggunakan future continuous untuk aksi yang sedang berlangsung pada waktu tertentu di masa depan dan untuk pertanyaan sopan tentang rencana.
objectives: Describe actions in progress at a specific future time
Ask politely about other people's plans
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Form
**will be + verb-ing** (negative: *won't be + -ing*).

| Type | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Positive | This time tomorrow, I **will be flying** to Jayapura. |
| Negative | Don't call at 9 — we **won't be working** then. |
| Question | **Will** you **be using** the car tonight? |

### Use 1: an action in progress at a future moment
Imagine a photo taken at a specific time in the future. What will be happening in the photo?
- *At 8 p.m. tonight, I'll be watching the final.*
- *In 2050, many people **will be living** in smart cities.*

Compare: *When you arrive, I'll cook dinner* (I'll start cooking after you arrive) vs. *When you arrive, I'll be cooking dinner* (I'll already be in the middle of cooking).

### Use 2: things that will happen as a matter of course
The future continuous can describe events that will happen anyway, as part of a normal routine or plan, not because of a new decision.
- *I'll be seeing Maya at the meeting tomorrow, so I can give her the book.*
- *The train **will be stopping** at all stations to Westport.* (typical in announcements)

### Use 3: polite questions about plans
Asking *Will you be + -ing?* sounds less direct than *Will you...?* because it asks about plans, not about willingness.
- *Will you be using the printer this afternoon?* (polite — I might want to use it)
- *Will you use the printer?* (can sound like a request or an order)

### Time expressions
*this time tomorrow / next week, at 6 p.m. tomorrow, in ten years' time, in 2050, all day tomorrow, when you arrive*

### Stative verbs again
As with other continuous forms, avoid *know, believe, own, want*: *In 2050, people will own fewer cars* (NOT *will be owning*).

> **Catatan:** Future continuous mirip dengan "akan sedang ..." dalam bahasa Indonesia: *Besok jam 8 saya **sedang** terbang ke Jayapura.* Dalam bahasa Inggris kita wajib memakai **will be + -ing**, bukan *will fly*. Pertanyaan *Will you be ...-ing?* adalah cara halus untuk menanyakan rencana seseorang.

lessons.title: Future Perfect: By 2050...
lessons.summary: Menggunakan future perfect (simple dan continuous) untuk hal yang sudah selesai atau sudah berlangsung sampai titik tertentu di masa depan.
objectives: Form the future perfect simple (will have + past participle)
Use by, by the time and before with the future perfect
Use the future perfect continuous to describe duration up to a future point
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Future perfect simple: completed before a future time
**will have + past participle** (negative: *won't have + past participle*).

Imagine standing at a point in the future and looking back. The action is already finished at that point.
- *By 2050, scientists **will have developed** new treatments for many diseases.*
- *Don't worry — I **will have finished** the report by Friday.*
- *They **won't have arrived** by six; the traffic is terrible.*

### Key time expressions
| Expression | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| by + time | not later than | **By** next June, I'll have graduated. |
| by the time + present simple | before/when | **By the time** you **get** home, I'll have cooked dinner. |
| in + period | after a period from now | **In** five years, the city will have doubled in size. |

⚠️ After *by the time / when / before*, use the **present simple**, not *will*: *By the time you **arrive*** (NOT *will arrive*).

### Future perfect continuous: duration up to a future point
**will have been + -ing** stresses how long an activity will have continued at a future moment.
- *Next month, Grandpa **will have been teaching** at the same school for forty years.*
- *By the time the plane lands, we'**ll have been travelling** for 18 hours.*

### Comparing future forms
| Form | Focus | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| future continuous | in progress at a future time | *At 10, I'll be writing.* |
| future perfect simple | finished before a future time | *By 10, I'll have written it.* |
| future perfect continuous | duration up to a future time | *By 10, I'll have been writing for three hours.* |

### Questions
*Will you **have finished** by lunchtime? How long **will** you **have been living** here by next year?*

> **Catatan:** Future perfect sering diterjemahkan sebagai "sudah ... (pada waktu tertentu di masa depan)": *Pada tahun 2030, kota ini **sudah** membangun jalur MRT baru* → *By 2030, the city **will have built** a new metro line.* Ingat: *by* = paling lambat, bukan 'oleh' dalam konteks ini.

lessons.title: Be About To, Be Due To, Be Likely To
lessons.summary: Mengungkapkan masa depan dekat, jadwal, dan kemungkinan dengan be about to, be due to, be likely to, dan be bound to.
objectives: Use be about to for the very near future
Use be due to for scheduled or expected events
Use be likely/unlikely to and be bound to to express probability and certainty
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Four useful structures
All of these use **be + adjective/word + to-infinitive**, and *be* changes for the subject and tense.

| Structure | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| be about to + inf | will happen very soon (in moments) | Hurry! The film **is about to start**. |
| be due to + inf | is scheduled/expected at a certain time | The train **is due to arrive** at 10:15. |
| be likely to + inf | will probably happen | Prices **are likely to rise**. |
| be unlikely to + inf | will probably not happen | She**'s unlikely to win**. |
| be bound to + inf | is certain to happen (speaker's opinion) | You**'re bound to pass**. You've worked so hard. |

### be about to
- Refers to the immediate future, so we normally **don't add a time expression** like *tomorrow*: *The meeting is about to begin* (✓), *The meeting is about to begin next week* (✗).
- Past form: *was/were about to* = something was going to happen, often interrupted: *I was about to call you when your message arrived.*

### be due to / be due
- *be due to + infinitive*: *The new hospital is due to open in March.*
- *be due + time/noun*: *The baby is due in May. The rent is due on Friday.*
- Don't confuse with **due to + noun** = because of: *The flight was delayed due to fog.*

### be likely to / it is likely that
Two patterns with the same meaning:
- *Prices **are likely to** rise.* = *It **is likely that** prices will rise.*
- Add adverbs for nuance: *very likely, highly unlikely, quite likely*.

### be bound to
Used when the speaker feels sure: *There's so much traffic — we're bound to be late.* It is stronger than *likely to*.

> **Catatan:** *be about to* = "sebentar lagi akan"; *be due to* = "dijadwalkan akan"; *be likely to* = "kemungkinan besar akan"; *be bound to* = "pasti akan". Jangan lupa **to** setelah *about, due, likely, bound*: ✗ *The bus is about leave.*

mistakes.right: The bus is about to leave.
mistakes.why: Be about must be followed by to + infinitive.

mistakes.wrong: The concert is about to start next Saturday.

mistakes.why: Be about to refers to the immediate future and doesn't take a future time expression; for a scheduled time use be due to.

mistakes.why: Be likely is followed by to + infinitive.

questions.explanation: All five expressions are followed by **to + infinitive**. They differ in timing (about to), scheduling (due to) and degree of certainty (likely, bound, unlikely).

lessons.title: Vocabulary: Science, Cities and Society
lessons.summary: Kosakata tentang sains, perkotaan, dan masyarakat untuk membicarakan masa depan.
objectives: Use vocabulary about cities, technology and population change
Use common collocations such as make a breakthrough and renewable energy
Describe future trends using the new vocabulary with future forms
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Cities of the future
| Word | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| urbanisation | the movement of people from rural areas to cities | Rapid **urbanisation** puts pressure on housing. |
| infrastructure | basic systems: roads, transport, water, power | The city must invest in **infrastructure**. |
| overcrowded | with too many people | **Overcrowded** trains are a daily problem. |
| sustainable | able to continue without harming the environment | We need **sustainable** transport. |
| renewable energy | energy from sources that don't run out (sun, wind) | **Renewable energy** will power most homes. |

### Science and technology
| Word | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| breakthrough | an important discovery | Scientists have **made a breakthrough** in battery design. |
| automation | using machines to do work people used to do | **Automation** will change many jobs. |
| artificial intelligence (AI) | computer systems that can learn and decide | **AI** is likely to transform healthcare. |
| cutting-edge | the most advanced | **cutting-edge** research |

### Society and population
| Word | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| life expectancy | the average age people live to | **Life expectancy** has been rising. |
| ageing population | a population with a growing share of older people | An **ageing population** needs more care workers. |
| inequality | an unfair difference between groups | Technology could reduce or increase **inequality**. |
| carbon emissions | CO₂ released into the air | Cities must cut **carbon emissions**. |

### Collocations to learn as chunks
- **make** a breakthrough / **make** a discovery
- **cut / reduce** emissions
- **invest in** infrastructure
- life expectancy **rises / increases**
- **tackle** inequality / climate change

### Word formation
*urban → urbanisation; automate → automation; sustain → sustainable → sustainability; equal → inequality; expect → expectancy*. Recognising suffixes (*-isation, -ation, -able, -ity*) helps you guess meaning in reading texts.

> **Catatan:** Ejaan Inggris Britania memakai *-ise/-isation* (urbanisation), sedangkan Amerika memakai *-ize/-ization* (urbanization); keduanya benar asalkan konsisten. *Ageing* (UK) = *aging* (US).

questions.explanation: *Angka harapan hidup* = **life expectancy** (not *life expectation*). *Terus meningkat* = *keeps rising / continues to rise*.

lessons.title: Making Predictions with Confidence
lessons.summary: Membuat prediksi dengan tingkat keyakinan yang berbeda-beda.
objectives: Express different degrees of certainty about the future
Place adverbs such as probably and definitely correctly
Combine future forms to make detailed predictions about 2050
lessons.completionCriteria: Complete the speaking task and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Selesaikan tugas berbicara dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### A scale of certainty
Good predictions show **how sure** you are.

| Certainty | Expressions |
| --- | --- |
| 100% | will definitely / certainly; be bound to; I'm convinced that... |
| ~75% | will probably; be likely to; may well; there's a good chance that... |
| ~50% | might; could; may; it's possible that... |
| ~25% | probably won't; be unlikely to; I doubt (that)...; there's little chance that... |
| 0% | definitely won't; there's no way that... (informal) |

### Adverb position
With **will**, the adverb goes *after* will in positive sentences but *before* won't in negative sentences:
- ✓ *It **will probably** rain.* / ✓ *It **probably won't** rain.*
- ✗ *It won't probably rain.*
- ✓ *We'll **definitely** need more doctors.* / ✓ *We **definitely won't** need petrol stations.*

### may well
*May well* means 'it is quite likely', stronger than *may* alone: *Robots **may well** replace many factory workers.*

### Combining future forms for detail
A detailed prediction often mixes forms from this unit:
- **future continuous** for situations in progress: *People **will be working** from home more.*
- **future perfect** for completed changes: *Petrol cars **will have disappeared** from many cities.*
- **be likely/bound to** for probability: *Food **is likely to become** more expensive.*

### Hedging: sounding careful
In academic or formal English, writers avoid sounding too certain:
- *It seems likely that...* / *There is evidence that... may...* / *According to some forecasts,...*

### Responding to predictions
| Agree | Disagree politely |
| --- | --- |
| *I think you're right.* | *I'm not so sure about that.* |
| *That's very likely.* | *I can't see that happening.* |

> **Catatan:** Kesalahan umum penutur bahasa Indonesia: menaruh *probably* setelah *won't* (✗ *won't probably*). Ingat pola: **will probably** dan **probably won't**. *I doubt* sudah bermakna negatif, jadi jangan tambah *not*: *I doubt cars will disappear* (bukan *I doubt cars won't...* jika maksudnya 'saya ragu mobil akan hilang').

examples.en: Cities will definitely be hotter in 2050.
examples.id: Kota-kota pasti akan lebih panas pada tahun 2050.

examples.en: Flying taxis may well be common by then.
examples.id: Taksi terbang bisa jadi sudah umum pada saat itu.

examples.en: I doubt that people will stop using paper completely.
examples.id: Saya ragu orang akan berhenti memakai kertas sepenuhnya.

examples.en: Most people probably won't own a car in the city centre.
examples.id: Kebanyakan orang mungkin tidak akan memiliki mobil di pusat kota.

vocabulary.example: Economic forecasts are often wrong.
Prices may well fall next year.
I'm convinced that AI will change education.
I doubt we'll live on Mars by 2050.
The trend towards remote work is likely to continue.

grammar.example: There's a good chance that it'll snow.

mistakes.why: Probably goes before won't in negative sentences.

mistakes.wrong: The new airport is likely opening in 2031.
mistakes.right: The new airport is likely to open in 2031.
mistakes.why: Be likely is followed by to + infinitive.

mistakes.wrong: I'm doubt that we'll live on Mars by 2050.
mistakes.right: I doubt that we'll live on Mars by 2050.
mistakes.why: Doubt is a verb here, so don't add am/is (saya ragu = I doubt).

sections.summary: Show your level of certainty with **definitely, bound to, probably, likely to, may well, might, unlikely to, I doubt**. Put *probably/definitely* **after will** but **before won't**. Combine future continuous, future perfect and *likely to* for detailed predictions, and hedge in formal writing. *Ringkasan: prediksi yang baik selalu menunjukkan seberapa yakin kita.*

reviewCards.back: Adverb position: after will, before won't

questions.prompt: Choose the expression that fits the context.
questions.instructions: Hint: the speaker is completely sure because it happens every year.
questions.text: Train fares ___ go up in January. They always do.
questions.explanation: *They always do* shows the speaker is certain, so **are bound to** (pasti akan) is correct. The other options express doubt.

questions.prompt: Put the fragments in order to make a prediction.
fragments: petrol cars will have disappeared completely.
questions.explanation: Time phrase → prediction with *will probably* → contrast with *but I doubt that* + future perfect (*will have disappeared*).

questions.prompt: Make at least three predictions about life in your city in 2050 (transport, work, housing or technology). Show how certain you are, and use at least one future continuous and one future perfect form.
questions.sampleAnswer: In 2050, I think most people in my city will be working from home at least two days a week. The city will probably have built a proper metro system by then, so traffic is likely to be much lighter. Housing may well become even more expensive, because more people will have moved here from rural areas. However, I doubt that flying cars will be common; they're too dangerous and expensive.
questions.explanation: A strong answer combines future forms (*will be working, will have built*) with different degrees of certainty (*probably, likely to, may well, I doubt*).

questions.prompt: Find the error.
questions.explanation: *Be likely* is followed by **to + infinitive**: *The new airport is likely to open in 2031.*

questions.prompt: Which sentences say that it will PROBABLY snow (but the speaker is not completely sure)? Select all that apply.
options: There's a good chance it'll snow.
questions.explanation: *Likely to, may well* and *there's a good chance* = probably. *Bound to* = certain (100%), and *I doubt* = probably not.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: She probably won't come to the conference.
She won't probably come to the conference.
She will come probably not to the conference.
She probably will not to come to the conference.
questions.explanation: In negative sentences, *probably* comes **before** *won't*: **She probably won't come.**

questions.prompt: Complete with ONE word: "There's a good ___ that the project will be finished early."
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is **There's a good chance (that)...** = it is quite likely.

unitTestQuestions.context: This time next month, I ___ in our new office in Port Selatan.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *This time next month* describes an action in progress at a future time → **will be working**.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
unitTestQuestions.text: By the time you get this postcard, we ___ (leave) the island.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: The leaving will be completed before a future moment (*by the time you get this postcard*) → **will have left**.

dialogue.speaker: Ana
dialogue.text: Is the new library open yet?

options: Not yet, but it's due to open next month.
Not yet, but it's due open next month.
Not yet, but it's about to open next month.
Not yet, but it's bound open next month.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: A scheduled future event → **be due to + infinitive**. *Be about to* is not used with a time expression like *next month*, and the other options are missing *to*.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using the word in brackets.
unitTestQuestions.sentence: I'm sure the meeting will run late. (bound)
answers: The meeting is bound to run late.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *I'm sure ... will* = **be bound to + infinitive**: *The meeting is bound to run late.*

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
acceptedAnswers: Most people will have moved to cities by 2050
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *By + time* + subject + **will have + past participle**: *By 2050, most people will have moved to cities.*

segments: my parents will have been married
so we will be organised a big party.
unitTestQuestions.correction: so we will be organising a big party.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: The future continuous needs the -ing form: **will be organising** (sedang menyiapkan). *Will have been married for thirty years* is correct (state up to a future point).

unitTestQuestions.prompt: What does the word in bold mean?
unitTestQuestions.context: Most experts agree that the new material is a genuine **breakthrough** that could make solar panels much cheaper.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: A **breakthrough** is an important discovery or development (terobosan).
